findings.reason: without the declared edge the queue treats §8 as ready now, and the dispatch that runs it spends a full measure to rediscover a stall the plan already knows and has a section for, which is the same defect the earlier review answered for s15.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s8: [s2, s3, s4, s5, s7, s15]` and no `s16` entry, yet followup f-aprop-003 is titled "Implement §16, then re-measure §8" (line 182), its body says §16 makes one call decode the index once "and §8's measure is then taken again" (line 183), and the s8 comment c-land-s8-measure says "the why view never answers; §16 owns that" (line 342) — so a scheduler can admit and launch §8 before §16 lands, and its "what blocks a named section" question then fails for exactly the reason §16 repairs; the ordering is stated in prose in three places and declared in none

findings.reason: a node told to run "one CLI why call" either takes on a second deliverable (a new CLI verb) that no section of this plan costs, or records the arm against a surface the done-when did not name; naming `read_plan(view="why")` as the call, which is the surface §8's measure already used, removes the ambiguity for one line of change.
findings.text: §16's third arm reads "One CLI why call on the power_convertor mount answers within the 30 s read deadline", but the why view has no CLI verb at this revision: `reckon/cli.py` imports its verbs explicitly and registers no `why`, the only consumers of `reckon/why_view.py` are `reckon/mcp.py` and `reckon/mcp_views.py`, the docstring of `why_view.py` states the surface as `read_plan(view="why", ...)`, and the `roadmap` verb takes `(project, sprint, checkout_path, max_paths, json_output, brief, since)` with no view option — so the arm can only be satisfied by adding a CLI surface §16 never scopes, or by quietly meaning the MCP call

findings.reason: the falsifying measurement exists in the section's own landing comment, so the record carries the control even though one of its two statements of it is vacuous; the section is landed and nothing a node does turns on which sentence a reader believes.
findings.text: §15's negative control is recorded twice with different results in the unit under review: the s15 landing comment says `tests/test_read_plan_answers_a_followup_wait.py` "reads 25 passed at head 6ca488dea against 20 failed/5 passed at base 116da9e9f" (line 240), while the closing record for the same section says the "Coordinator armed pair at ac18a69a7: base runs no tests (the file is new), head 25 passed" (line 243) — the second reading is of a base arm that collects nothing, so on its own it cannot show the guard fires, and a later reader cannot tell which of the two describes the control

response_events.reason: §15 is landed and its landing comment carries the falsifying measurement (20 failed at base 116da9e9f, 25 passed at 6ca488dea); the closing record's armed base collects nothing only because the test file is new at that base, which it states, so a node reads nothing differently either way.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_waited_on_by` (reckon/why_view.py:363, called from the view builder at :118), `_section_edges` (why_view.py:180), `roadmap._section_scoped_edges`, `_plan_authored_state` (reckon/roadmap.py:171), `resources.resolve_resource` (reckon/resources.py:881) and `metadata_index._read_persisted_memo` (reckon/metadata_index.py:1986) all resolve, and the `#s8-measure` anchor exists in docs/evidence/archive/a-project-reads-as-one-picture-landed.html.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's third done-when arm names "one CLI why call", and no CLI verb reaches the why view at this revision, so the arm names a command the implementation node cannot run.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section's evidence pointer is the cumulative landed archive at a repository path, and the run's command, elapsed seconds and answer go into that fragment rather than a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §16 names no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag in a symbol or a comment, and its prose states the mechanism rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the root cause matches the evidence.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 carries one deliverable (one decode of the persisted index per call), and its two candidate mechanisms are a delegated implementation choice under a stated constraint, not two goals.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `plan-section-depends-on` gives §8 the dependencies s2, s3, s4, s5, s7 and s15 but not s16, though §8's re-measure cannot answer until §16 lands.
